children: Sterling could fall further against the euro as the Bank of England remains cautious about raising interest rates, TD Securities strategists say in a note. The BOE voted 6-3 to leave rates unchanged Thursday. The lack of a material shift in guidance or vote split was seen as a disappointment for rate rise pricing and sterling, they say. The BOE's signals on potential tightening appear more cautious compared to the European Central Bank, they say. U.K. fiscal and political risk premiums are also set to rebuild before October's budget while sterling could underperform the euro on any risk aversion, they say. The euro rises 0.2% to 0.8582 pounds and TD expects it go above 0.86 pounds in coming weeks. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
